chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from al-Mu'afa ibn Wahb from al-Saffan from al-'Ala' ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), regarding His Exalted's saying: 'For those who can afford it, there is a duty to carry out to the House of God,' he said: 'He must have what enables him to perform Hajj.' I said: 'If Hajj is presented to him and he feels shy (of the cost/effort),' he said: 'He is among those who can afford it, and why should he feel shy? Even if it is on a single-humped camel.' He said: 'If he is able to walk part of the way and ride part of the way, let him do so.'

key_terms.أَجْدَعَ: A camel with a cut ear (a specific type of mount, implying even a modest animal suffices)
key_terms.مَنِ اسْتَطَاعَ إِلَيْهِ سَبِيلًا: Whoever is able to find a way/path to it (condition of ability)
key_terms.يَكُونُ لَهُ مَا يَحُجُّ بِهِ: He must have what enables him to perform Hajj (possession of means)
key_terms.يَمْشِيَ بَعْضًا وَيَرْكَبَ بَعْضًا: Walk part and ride part (mixed mode of travel)

ai.seo_question: What constitutes sufficient ability for the obligatory Hajj in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies that 'ability' (istita'ah) for Hajj is determined by the possession of sufficient means, noting that mere shyness or hesitation does not exempt one from the obligation. The hadith further establishes that partial capability, such as walking part of the journey and riding the rest, satisfies the condition of ability. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on practical feasibility and the removal of unnecessary hardship in religious duties.
